schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Patch and minor for dev tooling: auto-merge once CI is green. These never reach the browser bundle, so the blast radius is the build itself - which CI proves.
Patch for runtime dependencies: auto-merge. Patches are the security-relevant channel and sitting on them is the actual risk.

Minor for runtime dependencies: PR, reviewed by a human. CI has no DOM or visual coverage yet, so a subtle rendering change would pass it unnoticed. Flip `automerge` to true once the visual layer from ADR-0010 exists.
Angular moves as one unit. A partial upgrade of the framework is never valid, and the whole set needs `ng update` migrations rather than a version bump.
prBodyNotes: :warning: Do not merge as a plain version bump. Run `ng update @angular/core@<major> @angular/cli@<major>` locally - it applies code migrations this PR does not contain.
Then walk the manual UI checklist in docs/adr/0010-dependency-policy.md.

packageRules.description: The two chess libraries render the board. Any change here is a visual change by definition.
prBodyNotes: :warning: Touches board rendering. Check coordinates, piece artwork, arrows/circles and the setup mini-board before merging.

packageRules.description: Every major is a manual decision, with no exception.
TypeScript is pinned by Angular's supported range; a bump outside it breaks the compiler in ways tsc reports late and confusingly.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security advisories bypass the schedule and the grouping. They still need CI green, and they still need a human for a major.
